Independent coefficient check: a Lomax law is a mixture of exponentials with gamma-distributed rate (shape alpha, rate ell). For rho=ell|omega| the ratio of the exact to leading small-omega coefficient is (2 sin(pi alpha/2)/pi) times integral x^(alpha-1) exp(-rho*x)/(1+x^2) dx on (0,infinity). Substituting x=exp(s) and composite Simpson on [-40,60] with spacing 0.01, ell=1.3, gives ratios 0.95195375 and 0.98087243 at alpha=1.8, |omega|=1e-7 and 1e-9, respectively. This avoids subtracting rounded cosines and is numerical corroboration only.
correctness.rationale: Integrating one curved flight produces the centered iid complex reward v exp(i Theta)(exp(i omega L)-1)/(i omega), with modulus at most 2v/|omega|. Its per-coordinate covariance is v^2 E[1-cos(omega L)]/omega^2 by isotropy. A functional CLT for the indexed rewards and the finite-mean renewal law of large numbers give a time change by 1/mu. The joint convergence does not require reward-duration independence because the limiting clock is deterministic. At equilibrium the delay is almost surely finite, and unfinished and initial arcs are uniformly negligible after rescaling; the same limit holds starting at a renewal. Zero covariance occurs exactly for full-circle-multiple durations. In equilibrium the velocity dot-product correlation is v^2 cos(omega s) E[(L-s)_+]/mu; after any renewal the two headings give zero expected dot product. Integrating by parts and using integrability of the fresh survival function gives E[1-cos(omega L)]/(mu omega^2) for the scalar residual-survival cosine integral, even when the original cosine integral is only conditionally convergent. The planar MSD slope is 4D. For Lomax, rescaling its density and dominating by (1-cos y)y^(-1-alpha) gives the stated positive gamma factor for 1<alpha<2. At omega=0 the equilibrium residual survival is (1+s/ell)^(1-alpha); the integrated correlation then gives the stated t^(3-alpha) law with the beta-integral prefactor. This last asymptotic is for equilibrium preparation, not a claim of the same prefactor after a fresh start.
residual_risks: Fixed nonzero omega is taken before the long-time limit. There is no joint crossover theorem. The zero-curvature prefactor is not preparation-independent.

evidence: The straight Lévy-walk limit starts at a renewal and has stable rather than Gaussian scaling for the indexed tail range, with the t^(3-alpha) second-moment exponent. The review treats arbitrary finite-mean straight renewal laws at equilibrium through the residual-life integral.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The straight-flight theorems and generic reward-process CLTs provide comparison and methods. A curved arc reward is bounded and may vanish identically on arithmetic supports; the characteristic-function diffusivity and weak-curvature asymptotic require identifying and evaluating that new reward.

evidence: For omega=0 substitution of the Lomax tail into the prior equilibrium residual survival and integration of the correlation gives the stated zero-curvature prefactor. The Poisson theory fixes an exponential clock and cannot take an infinite-variance clock specialization. A deterministic fixed-angle turn can retain heading coherence and is not a uniform refresh.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Do not credit the straight equilibrium consequence or Poisson case as new. The non-Poisson curved Gaussian/singular-diffusivity statement couples a general finite-mean renewal time change to a model-specific bound on arc rewards; the resulting exact variance and small-curvature divergence are not an available specialization of the inspected prior results.

evidence: For L exponential with rate lambda, the frozen formula reduces to v^2 lambda/[2(lambda^2+omega^2)]. With zero rotational diffusion and uniform tumble angles, the earlier Poisson model has the same correlation and variance slope. Its D defined by radial MSD over 2t is twice the per-coordinate D here.

The reviewed stationary straight-walk survival is the same integrated fresh survival divided by the mean; one-dimensional and planar straight iid refresh give the same dot-product correlation at identical speed and survival.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These are exact equivalences on the Poisson and straight stationary slices, after normalizing diffusion and matching preparations; neither gives the nonzero-curvature finite-mean theorem.

originality.rationale: The Poisson diffusivity, equilibrium residual-life formula, classical straight Lévy-walk behavior and general invariance-principle machinery are prior. The supported distinct increment is the fixed-curvature functional Gaussian result with its exact diffusivity for arbitrary independent finite-mean renewal durations under uniform refresh, including degeneracy, and the quantitative singular diffusivity as curvature vanishes for Lomax flights. The zero-curvature equilibrium MSD is a classical-renewal comparison, not standalone novelty.
residual_risks: Bounded best-of-knowledge comparison; equivalent results may exist under semi-Markov transport or regenerative velocity correlation formulations.

value.rationale: A finite-mean heavy-tailed flight clock can generate either superdiffusion or a finite-variance Brownian limit in essentially the same continuous trajectory model. Full circular flight closure, not a change of renewal law, accounts for the difference and for the arithmetic degeneracy. The exact diffusivity and power-law blowup quantify why convergence at fixed curvature cannot be interpreted as a regular zero-curvature limit.
residual_risks: Does not establish the crossover time or address arbitrary heading correlations or rotational diffusion.
